script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Workplace
Theme: second chances

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

EXT. SUNNY CALIFORNIA STREET - DAY

A calm, sunny morning. Vibrant colors of nature bursting forth in the quintessential Californian neighborhood. Birds chirping. A few children playing in the distance. The hustle and bustle of people going about their day.

INT. SMALL COFFEE SHOP - DAY

The warm, welcoming interior of a quaint coffee shop. SARAH, early 30s, with an air of quiet determination, sits at a table, sipping coffee. Her expression is thoughtful as she revises her resume. The door creaks open, and a new customer enters.

INT. SMALL COFFEE SHOP - DAY (CONT'D)

JASON, mid-30s, a disheveled, desperate-looking man enters, his eyes scanning the room for any sign of hope. He approaches the counter, looking for a familiar face. He spots Sarah and tentatively makes his way over to her table.

JASON
(timidly)
Hey, mind if I join you? I'm Jason. I used to work here a few years ago.

SARAH (pauses, considering)
(smiling)
Hi, Jason. It's nice to see you again. Sure, you can sit down.

INT. SMALL COFFEE SHOP - DAY (CONT'D)

Jason takes a seat across from Sarah. They make small talk as Jason tells her about his recent hardships. Sarah listens intently, offering him words of encouragement.

JASON
I've made some mistakes in the past. Lost my job, lost my home, and now I'm on the streets. But I'm determined to turn my life around.

SARAH
(gently)
It's never too late to start over, Jason. I've made mistakes in my past, too. But with hard work and perseverance, you can find a new path.

INT. SMALL COFFEE SHOP - DAY (CONT'D)

The coffee shop door creaks open, and in walks MARK, the coffee shop owner. He greets Sarah and Jason, and they engage in friendly banter. Mark mentions a vacancy in his shop and suggests that Jason apply for the position.

MARK
(to Jason)
You know what, Jason? I've got an opening for a part-time barista. Why don't you give it a shot?

JASON
(surprised)
Really? I'd be grateful for the opportunity, Mark.

INT. SMALL COFFEE SHOP - DAY (CONT'D)

Sarah and Jason continue their conversation, with Sarah sharing her experiences and offering Jason advice. Mark approaches their table and hands Jason an application.

MARK
(to Jason)
Here you go. Fill it out and bring it back to me tomorrow. I'll give it a look and get back to you.

INT. SMALL COFFEE SHOP - DAY (CONT'D)

Sarah and Jason exchange heartfelt goodbyes as he leaves the coffee shop. She watches him go, feeling a sense of hope for his future.

INT. SMALL COFFEE SHOP - LATER (NIGHT)

The coffee shop is closing down for the day. Sarah sits at the counter, sipping her coffee, deep in thought. She looks up as the door creaks open, and in walks Jason, looking exhausted but determined.

JASON
(weary)
Hey, Sarah. I filled out the application and I'd like to know if you could take a look at it before I submit it tomorrow.

SARAH
(smiling)
Of course, Jason. I'd be happy to help you out.

INT. SMALL COFFEE SHOP - LATER (NIGHT) (CONT'D)

Sarah reads through Jason's application, offering suggestions and advice. He listens intently, absorbing every word. They continue this process for the next few hours, with Sarah helping Jason craft a compelling resume.

INT. SMALL COFFEE SHOP - DAY (NEXT DAY)

The sun streams in through the coffee shop windows as Sarah and Jason arrive. They enter the coffee shop to find Mark behind the counter, looking over a stack of applications.

MARK
(to Jason)
Jason, I'm glad you came in early. I've got good news for you. I've read through all the applications, and yours stood out. You've got the job.

JASON
(ecstatic)
Really? That's amazing! I can't believe it!

INT. SMALL COFFEE SHOP - DAY (CONT'D)

Sarah and Jason celebrate Jason's new job, with Mark joining in on the festivities. They discuss the future and the importance of second chances.

MARK
(to Jason)
Sarah was a big help in getting your application ready. She's got a great heart and a wonderful attitude.

SARAH
(blushing)
It was my pleasure, Mark. I'm glad we could help each other out.

INT. SMALL COFFEE SHOP - DAY (CONT'D)

Jason starts his new job, and Sarah continues to support him. They become fast friends and confidants, offering each other encouragement and guidance as they move forward in their lives.

FADE OUT.

End screenplay.
